title: PATCH-103: BzkAdaptiveSolver runtime on 20K-face mesh — PCG iters per pin grow with mesh scale
description:
Phase A rewrite (BzkSystem + BzkAdaptiveSolver + GreedyRounding) is structurally correct: rocker-arm without PATCH-96 constraints gives 34 singularities (metriko=32, paper=36). But runtime is 2.7 hours due to 10.9M total CG iterations across 10046 chord pins.

Breakdown:
- bootstrap (cold start from x=0): 500-1000+ PCG iters
- per-pin re-solves (warm start): avg 1085 iters/pin

Both worse than expected because Jacobi preconditioning still leaves a poorly conditioned matrix on a real (non-spherical) 20K-face mesh.

Two fixes to investigate:

1. INCOMPLETE CHOLESKY (IC0/ICT) preconditioner: replaces M=diag(A) with sparse approximate Cholesky factor. 5-10x fewer iters expected.

2. SPARSE-RESIDUAL WARM START: after committing pin c, residual is nonzero only at neighbors of c. Currently PCG ignores this and does full global iteration. Track local residual support to short-circuit when the change is contained.

Combined target: rocker-arm full recompute < 60s.
definition-of-done: rocker-arm full bench with -Dixdar.lyon.recomputeField=true completes in < 60s; 92/92 quadlayout regression green.
testing-plan: Re-run BenchmarkRockerArmLyon with -Dixdar.lyon.principalTau=Infinity, confirm < 60s; verify singularity count stays in [30, 40] range.
